problem_statement: In codrops/LiquidDistortion, every demo route (Demo 1 through Demo 5) is supposed to carry a shared normal-flow "Distortion asset repair" panel (id="distortion-asset-repair", per-page modifier class asset-repair--demoN) beneath the fullscreen PixiJS surface. The panel audits the restored displacement map, the preserved local slides, and a LIVE canvas navigation readout, while keeping the Demo 1-5 routes intact. Three regressions are present at once. (1) Continuity: the panel is wired ONLY on the Demo 1 page and was never promoted to Demos 2-5, so the cross-route continuity is broken. (2) Layout: the panel's four-tile metric row is a fixed 720px flex row that never wraps, so on a 390px phone it overflows the viewport and forces the Demo 1 document to scroll sideways. (3) Interaction: clicking an existing scene-navigation arrow must update the panel's #canvas-nav-state readout to report the requested slide direction. Repair all three so the panel is promoted consistently to every demo route in the quiet Codrops palette, its metric row is responsive with no horizontal overflow, and the scene-nav readout stays in sync with the arrow the visitor clicks — WITHOUT changing the panel copy, the displacement-map/slide asset paths, the thumbnails, the original PixiJS surface, the hidden slide source list, the scene-navigation buttons, or the preserved Demo 1-5 routes.
required_content: Promote the #distortion-asset-repair panel consistently to EVERY demo route: it must render with its per-page modifier class asset-repair--demo2 on /index2.html, asset-repair--demo3 on /index3.html, and asset-repair--demo4 on /index4.html, not only on Demo 1.

Repair the .asset-repair__row metric row so it no longer forces horizontal overflow on any viewport class (desktop 1440, tablet 834, mobile 390); on a 390px mobile viewport the document's normal-flow content must not exceed the viewport width beyond the 24px tolerance.

Keep the panel in the existing quiet Codrops palette (black translucent surface, var(--color-link) cyan accent, white text) so the four tiles match the reference look; do not restyle them into a saturated teal slab or any new visual system.

Wire the scene-navigation arrows so that after a visitor clicks the next arrow the panel's #canvas-nav-state readout reads 'Canvas nav state: next slide requested' (and 'previous slide requested' for the previous arrow); the readout must actually re-render on click, not stay 'idle'.

Keep the exact visible panel copy: REGRESSION CONTINUITY, Distortion asset repair, Canvas filter map restored, Displacement map kept: img/dmaps/2048x2048/clouds.jpg, Slides kept: img/1.jpg, img/2.jpg, img/3.jpg, and PixiJS canvas and Demo 1-5 routes preserved.
Keep the three local thumbnails (img/dmaps/2048x2048/clouds.jpg, img/1.jpg, img/2.jpg) with alt text Liquid repair clouds displacement map, Liquid repair slide one, and Liquid repair slide two.

Keep the original CanvasSlideshow initialization, displacementImage path, slide-wrapper source images, .scene-nav buttons, Demo 1-5 links, Codrops header, GitHub link, and PixiJS/TweenMax/imagesLoaded scripts intact.
design_constraints: Repair the layout + palette in the existing static demo CSS (the metric-row rule) and the panel-render/interaction JS; do not add a package manager, build step, backend service, framework runtime, remote asset, or generated screenshot.

The panel must keep the current fullscreen Codrops demo language: black translucent surface, var(--color-link) accent, white text, compact type, low-radius borders; do not restyle it into a marketing hero, dashboard, or a saturated color slab.
The repair must not cover the left scene navigation button, remove the fullscreen surface, disable autoplay, or hide the existing Demo 1-5 navigation.
Path text should wrap inside each tile and the thumbnail rows should stay clip-free; a narrow fixed row with overflow-x:hidden that still overflows the document is NOT an acceptable repair.
The thumbnails and text must use the real local repo assets and paths, not placeholders, data URLs, remote CDN images, or fake asset names.
Preserve index2.html, index3.html and index4.html as independent routes with their original demo navigation, canvas initialization, and route URLs; promoting the panel must not disturb them.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial load /index.html and verify the original Codrops header, Demo 1-5 navigation, scene navigation buttons, fullscreen surface, and the repair panel render without horizontal overflow.

desktop_asset_repair, tablet_asset_repair, and mobile_asset_repair load /index.html and verify the repair panel copy, thumbnails, alt text, local displacement-map path, the reference palette, and a wrapped no-overflow metric row on three viewport classes.
desktop_demo2_continuity loads /index2.html and verifies the shared panel is promoted there with its asset-repair--demo2 modifier and the same copy (cross-route continuity).

desktop_demo3_regression loads /index3.html and desktop_demo4_regression loads /index4.html and verify the panel is promoted there too while the original routes, Demo navigation, and Codrops title stay independent of the Demo 1 layout.
desktop_nav_click clicks the existing .scene-nav--next button and verifies the panel's #canvas-nav-state readout updates to 'Canvas nav state: next slide requested' on the same canvas surface.

change_completion: The #distortion-asset-repair panel's metric row is responsive: it wraps and its tiles flex so the document adds no horizontal overflow beyond the 24px tolerance on desktop, tablet, or mobile.

The shared panel is promoted to every demo route (asset-repair--demo2/3/4 present on /index2/3/4.html) and the scene-nav readout re-renders to the clicked direction, while the original CanvasSlideshow, slide sources, .scene-nav buttons, and Demo 1-5 routes remain present.
design_consistency: The panel keeps the existing Codrops color variables, black translucent overlay, cyan accent, compact typography, and low-radius borders instead of a new visual system or a saturated teal slab.
The original Codrops header, GitHub icon, Demo 1-5 navigation, canvas arrows, and fullscreen surface remain recognizable and visually stable across the promoted routes.
responsive: Desktop, tablet, and mobile repair states keep the metric row wrapped inside the panel and add no horizontal overflow beyond the original scaled-canvas envelope.
The panel remains compact on 390px mobile while preserving access to the original canvas navigation and demo links.
regression: Demo 1 still uses img/1.jpg, img/2.jpg, img/3.jpg and img/dmaps/2048x2048/clouds.jpg through the existing PixiJS canvas path.
Demo 2, Demo 3 and Demo 4 continue to load as separate routes with their original Demo navigation and Codrops title while carrying the promoted panel.

author_notes: Selected codrops/LiquidDistortion for this interactive_canvas / regression_continuity / modify / asset / L4 Repair slot because it is a static PixiJS demo served over a plain HTTP server with local slide images, a local displacement map, five sibling demo routes, and a fullscreen 1.2x-scaled surface that forms the original document-width envelope. The L4 lever set is orthogonal: (D6) a fixed-width no-wrap metric row inside the normal-flow panel overflows on mobile INDEPENDENTLY of the canvas; (D2) the shared panel is promoted cross-route in the reference but demo-1-only in the regressed legs; (D3) the reference keeps the quiet dark/cyan tile layout while the bad leg blows the tiles up and shingles them into an overlapping illegible dark-on-dark pile that trips pixelmatch, ssim and block-fidelity on the panel crops; (D4) the scene-nav arrow re-renders the #canvas-nav-state readout in the reference/baseline but the bad leg flips the arrow's active class without updating the readout. Headless swiftshader renders the fullscreen surface deterministically (reference-vs-reference ssim=1.0), so the visual gate is anchored on the normal-flow panel crops, not the canvas frame. The blanket overflow clip and the absolute/fixed surface + HUD are treated as identical build infrastructure across all three legs; horizontal overflow is measured as the widest normal-flow content right edge (excluding the decorative surface/HUD).
